key_provisions_or_claims: Calls for banning AI to propose judicial decisions and predictive policing of individuals
Calls for permanent prohibition of biometric recognition in public spaces and a moratorium on facial recognition identification
Requires mandatory fundamental rights impact assessments and periodic independent audits
Insists final decisions with legal effect be taken by humans, with clear liability on natural or legal persons
Calls for transparency, auditable non-proprietary systems, and strict framework for police drones
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 6 October 2021 on AI in criminal law and its use by police and judicial authorities. It sets out fundamental-rights safeguards: bans on predictive policing of individuals, mass biometric surveillance and AI-proposed judicial decisions, a facial recognition moratorium, mandatory impact assessments, audits, transparency and human accountability.
annotation.title_clean: Artificial intelligence in criminal law and its use by the police and judicial authorities in criminal matters
